correctness.rationale: For f^{i+d}=f^i with d>0 the image under f^i is periodic and every cycle length divides d; the converse holds. Hence the first repeat is at h and h+p. A height≥2 map cannot be recovered from another power, while height zero and one give cyclic groups of order p (the latter with a nonambient identity), with φ(p) generators. This also validates the frozen partition sum and the divisor-Möbius height/period formula, which the repair no longer claims as contributions. The deficit is H_n−G_n, with H_n the count of height≤1 maps and G_n their reciprocal-totient weight. The cycle-of-stars series 1/(1−ze^z) has its unique nearest simple pole at ρ, with coefficient factor 1/(1+ρ). The periods of bounded totient form a finite set, whose shallow class is dominated by an entire restricted-cycle series. Outside that class the weight is arbitrarily small, proving G_n=o(H_n). Removing periods 1 and 2 separately proves that the count of maps with a second generator has the same equivalent, not the same exact count. Stirling gives the displayed exceptional probability. The replacement also removes the corrupted totient glyph in the frozen last proof paragraph.
residual_risks: Finite numbers check the definitions and exact inputs, not the sharp analytic limit. No formal proof or attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: Quantifying precisely how rarely the map-to-submonoid correspondence fails to be injective distinguishes a leading rate and constant from a generic exponential upper bound. The result also resolves the difference between the deficit, which weights each fiber by its excess size, and the number of affected maps. The finite-period bound genuinely controls the correction for the natural generator-collision question; the shared mapping-class pole by itself does not.
residual_risks: No secondary asymptotic terms or finer distributions of the number of alternative generators are asserted.
